predecessors.name: Alodia
predecessors.text: what was left of Alodia: Soba and the Gezira

successors.name: Muhammad Ali dynasty
successors.text: Sennar and the Gezira, held by Egypt from the surrender of Badi VII on 14 June 1821

ledger.x: 1504: the Funj Sultanate is founded.
1504: the Funj take Alodia's remnant.
1504: the Abdallabi become Funj vassals.
By 1523: the Funj hold Dongola.
1665: the Funj conquer Fazughli.

c. 1665: Taqali becomes a vassal. 'Under Badi II's rule the Funj defeated the Kingdom of Taqali to the west and made its ruler his vassal' (Funj page; Badi II reigned 1644/5-1681, so the year is a bridge). Rechecked against the Kordofan correction: Taqali lies in the Nuba Hills of South Kordufan, which the Taqali page…
1734: Isawi of the Musabba'at drives out the Ghudiyat.
1755: Abu Likayik overruns Kordofan.
1762: the Hamaj regency begins.
c. 1772: Hashim of the Musabba'at retakes Kordofan. 'Around 1772 Hashim of the Musabba'at led an insurgency which retook control of Kordofan from the aging Likaylik.'
1782: the Funj retake Kordofan.
c. 1782: Dongola falls to the Shaigiya. 'Dongola finally fell to the Shaykiyya in around 1782.'

c. 1785: the Fur take Kordofan. 'Around 1785 the Funj withdrew from Kordofan amid a civil war', then 'the elderly Tayrab launched an invasion' (Darfur page, infobox 'Conquest of Kordofan: c. 1785'); the Funj page says 1785/1786 and the Hamaj page 1787.
Second half of the 18th century: the Tigre of what is now Eritrea are lost.
1791: Taka makes itself independent ('after 1791 Taka around the Sudanese Mareb River made itself independent').
1802: the Funj are confined to the Gezira.
1821: the Abdallabi vassalage ends with the Egyptian conquest.
1821: the Taqali tribute to Sennar ends with the Egyptian invasion.
May 1821: the Egyptian army reaches the confluence.
14 June 1821: the last sultan surrenders.
June 1821: Egypt takes Sennar and the Gezira.
14 June 1821: the Funj Sultanate ends.

wars.name: Battle of Hannik (Funj-Ottoman frontier war)
wars.outcome: Funj victory: the Ottomans, who had reached 'as far south as the Third Cataract', were 'crushed by the Funj at the battle of Hannik' in 1585.

wars.name: Funj-Ethiopian wars
wars.outcome: A full-fledged war in 1618-1619 and a Funj army of 30,000-100,000 gathered on the Dinder River in March 1744; no border change the page names.

wars.name: Shilluk raids on the Funj
wars.outcome: 'From the mid-17th century onwards the Shilluk began raiding the Funj'; no border change the page names.

wars.name: Funj-Musabba'at struggle for Kordofan
wars.outcome: The Musabba'at under Isawi dislodged the Ghudiyat administration in 1734 and 'repelled subsequent Funj attempts to regain their foothold'; Abu Likayik overran Kordofan in 1755.

wars.name: Funj-Musabba'at-Fur contest for Kordofan
wars.outcome: Hashim retook Kordofan about 1772, the Funj ousted him in 1782, and about 1785 the Funj withdrew amid civil war and the Fur under Tayrab conquered it.

wars.name: Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory: Badi VII surrendered on 14 June 1821, Kordofan fell the same year, and 'by the beginning of 1822 all of riverine Sudan and Kordofan was under Egyptian control'.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the Third Cataract, the Ethiopian Highlands, the Nuba Mountains and the Gezira are the only limits named.
